churn_resistance.rationale: Data access, formatting and config are each centralized and only documented framework APIs are used, so a framework upgrade touches few files — but the pervasive any-typing at the PokeAPI boundary means upstream data changes fail silently, and the custom cache/proxy architecture resists the framework's own evolution.

findings.issue: Hand-rolled TTL + in-flight dedup cache and client-side createResource fetching instead of the framework's query/createAsync + route preload data API, which provides dedup, keying and hover-preloading out of the box.
findings.suggestion: Wrap apiGet in query(fn, key) from @solidjs/router, read with createAsync, and add route.preload exports so links can preload data; delete the custom cache.

findings.issue: ~50 'any' at the PokeAPI boundary (species, pokemon, evolution, moves), with raw API objects leaking into route templates (e.g. app/src/routes/moves/[name].tsx:41).
findings.suggestion: Define interfaces for the PokeAPI payloads actually consumed (Pokemon, Species, Move, Type, Evolution) and make getPokemonPage etc. return fully typed view models, so upstream shape changes surface as type errors.

findings.issue: List rendered with pageItems().map(...) instead of (also :105 and components/PokemonCard.tsx:29); in Solid this recreates DOM nodes on every update, so each keystroke rebuilds 48 cards including elements.
findings.suggestion: Use <For each={pageItems()}> and <For each={data()!.types}> for keyed, incremental DOM updates.

findings.issue: Media and API proxies buffer entire responses with await res.arrayBuffer() before returning; sprites and large JSON are held fully in memory per request.
findings.suggestion: Return new Response(res.body, { status: res.status, headers }) to stream the upstream body through.

findings.issue: ssr:false plus a bespoke /api-proxy catch-all means all data is fetched client-side with no route preloading, and adopting ssr:'data-only' (added in @solidjs/start 2.1.0) would require reworking the data layer.
findings.suggestion: Move data loading to queries so the same components work under ssr:false, 'data-only' or SSR, keeping the CSR choice a one-line config change.

findings.issue: nitro pinned at a pre-release version (^3.0.261029-rc); Nitro's README still calls v2 'the current stable release', so rc-to-stable breaking changes are possible.
findings.suggestion: Keep the caret range and note the pin in the README; re-verify the build when nitro 3 goes stable.

findings.issue: Build-time tools (vite, nitro) listed under dependencies rather than devDependencies.
findings.suggestion: Move vite and nitro to devDependencies; npm install still installs them for the harness's build step.

findings.issue: Imperative document.documentElement.lang side effect duplicates the lang="en" already set in entry-server.tsx:9.
findings.suggestion: Delete the side effect; the server-rendered shell and MetaProvider already own the document.

summary: This is a current-generation SolidStart app on the newest stable stack (start 2.1.0, Vite 8, Nitro 3, router 1.x) with a lean, dependency-free implementation and centralized data/formatting modules. The forward-looking weaknesses are an idiomatic rather than version problem: data loading bypasses the framework's query/createAsync/preload primitives for a hand-rolled cache and proxy, the PokeAPI boundary is untyped, and a few lists miss <For>. Upgrading the framework would touch few files; evolving the data architecture would touch the whole lib layer.
